text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
- Smallholder President Jozsef Torgyan was not an agent or informer of the communist secret services, a screening committee said.
- Union Workers' Council challanges the distribution of social insurance authority mandates.
- The Hungarian-Slovak Prime Ministerial meeting is expected to focus on the bilateral treaty and minority rights.
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn praised Romania for the handling of its Hungarian miniority and its reform endeavors.
- A Hungarian-Polish-Czech summitt will be held in Cracow, Poland, on August 22.
- Hungary's January-June overall trade deficit was over 200 billion forints.
- A CSFB study said Hungary's rating is likely to be improved in the next 12 months.
- Travel holding Ibusz posted a 76.9 million forints loss in the first half of 1997.
- German media group Bertelsmann offered $2.5 million for a 17.06 percent stake in national daily Nepszabadsag.
- Hungary's life insurance companies took in 28.14 billion forints of insurance premiums in the first half of 1997, up 27.6 percent over the same period of 1996.
